pages.text: A soft glow fills the room as Tara the television turns on. Bright pictures line up, ready to tell a story.
Pictures on Tara move smoothly. Many tiny images change very fast so our eyes see motion.
Sound comes with the pictures. Speakers inside Tara turn signals into voices, music, and effects.
Shows reach Tara through signals, cables, or the internet. Different paths bring the same fun.
A remote helps choose. Buttons send commands so Tara knows which show and volume to use.
Turning the volume knob changes loudness. Softer sound can be kinder to ears.
Television can teach and entertain. News, cartoons, and nature shows share ideas and facts.
Eyes and bodies need breaks. Standing up and stretching helps after watching.
Families choose together. Picking shows and times makes TV a helpful helper.
When the screen goes dark, Tara rests. Stories will return tomorrow, bright and ready.
